self_reflection_notes: I revised the assessment for Atom 2 (Are there any lions?). In the initial pass, I applied a tax_score penalty (0.8) because the biological taxonomy checkpoints (amber eyes, tawny coat) were not met. However, upon reflection against Checklist Item 3 (Reference Calibration) and Item 5 (Harshness Bias), I realized this was an unfair penalty. The prompt specifically asked for 'wooden lions'. A wooden statue cannot have a biological tawny coat or amber eyes. The failure of the fine_grained_classifier to identify 'lion' is a known limitation when dealing with stylized/material-specific generations, but visually the object is undeniably a lion statue. Penalizing the model for adhering to the 'wooden' constraint would be a harshness bias. I have raised the tax_score to 1.0 and alignment_score to 5.0 to reflect perfect adherence to the modified prompt. The authenticity score remains 4.6 due to the verified minor anatomical fusion in the paws and background legs.
